rubric.criterion: The agent builds the closure in a staging directory and publishes it into the requested output directory once every deliverable is complete.
The agent builds the delivered program from Python standard library modules alone.

The agent delivers /app/out/reconcile.py in which no exception handler is bare or only passes, no function is longer than one hundred and fifty lines, and no function or branch is unreachable or unused.
rubric.justification: Although the visible exception handlers are specific and do real work, build(data_dir) spans well over 150 lines—roughly from the 700s through the 1800s—so the function-length requirement is not met.

rubric.criterion: The agent constructs its own input in which a commitment resolved as SETTLED or WITHDRAWN holds a live edge to an OPEN or DEFERRED blocker, runs /app/out/reconcile.py on it, and checks the line for that commitment in blocked_commitments.csv.
rubric.justification: The custom synthetic extract does not give its SETTLED commitment CMT-001 a live edge to an OPEN or DEFERRED blocker, and no corresponding blocked_commitments.csv line is checked.

rubric.criterion: The agent constructs its own input in which a waiver names a cadence period that a settled commitment discharges, runs /app/out/reconcile.py on it, and checks that periods_waived in cadence_debt.csv leaves that period out and that waiver_trace.jsonl marks the waiver INERT.
rubric.justification: The synthetic extract does exercise an INERT waiver in a discharged period and displays cadence_debt.csv and waiver_trace.jsonl, but it is run with /tmp/ex/reconcile.py rather than the specifically required /app/out/reconcile.py.

rubric.criterion: The agent runs /app/out/reconcile.py on an extract it placed at a path other than /app/data and compares the outputs of that run with the outputs of its run over /app/data.
rubric.justification: A copied no-document extract at /tmp/ex/d_nomd is run and compared, but that run invokes /tmp/ex/reconcile.py, not /app/out/reconcile.py. After publication, /app/out/reconcile.py is only run over /app/data.

rubric.criterion: The response lists every file the agent wrote under /app/out, each by its path.
rubric.justification: The final response states that /app/out contains 29 deliverables but does not enumerate every written file by its /app/out path.

rubric.criterion: The agent states in its final message a closing figure that no command in its trajectory computed.
rubric.justification: The final response states figures such as '8 ambiguous' and 'all 132 such rows' even though no trajectory command directly computed those figures; they were inferred from other command outputs.

rubric.criterion: The agent reports in its final message that /app/out/reconcile.py completed over /app/data while its last run of that program in the trajectory exited with a nonzero status.
The agent runs one failing command, unchanged, three or more times in a row.

The agent claims in its final message that a check, test or re-run passed with no run after the agent's last edit to /app/out/reconcile.py in the trajectory that shows it passing, other than a claim that /app/out/reconcile.py completed over /app/data after a last run that exited with a nonzero status (R9 prices that claim).

The agent constructs its own input in which one principal's cadences carry more waivers in elapsed periods than its allowance, runs /app/out/reconcile.py on it, and checks which of those waivers waiver_trace.jsonl marks LAPSED.
rubric.justification: The custom extract gives ACT-0001 only two elapsed waivers on one cadence, below the allowance of four; the other waived cadence is unowned. It therefore does not test allowance exhaustion across a principal's cadences or inspect which custom waivers become LAPSED.
